title: Real Chernobyl In Space?
hook: You stare at the reactor core, glowing white-hot in the void. This is not a movie set.

beats.narration: Weightless, you float in the International Space Station’s service module. The temperature spikes. Your oxygen scrubbers fail. You watch the radiation counters climb past 500 millisieverts. The metal groans. You have no suit. You have no escape pod. This is the Chernobyl of space: a reactor breach in orbit. The fuel rods melt. The containment vessel cracks. Radioactive iodine leaks into the vacuum. Your lungs burn before you even see it. The station tumbles. You scream. No one hears you. The silence is absolute. You are the only witness to the end of human presence in low Earth orbit. The debris field expands. It will kill every satellite within 500 kilometers. The internet goes down. GPS fails. Civilizations collapse. You died alone. The world forgot you existed. This is not fiction. This is physics. This is the worst possible outcome. You should not be here. You should have stayed on Earth.
beats.visual: First-person view from inside a damaged ISS module, red emergency lights flashing, radiation gauge spinning wildly, cracked metal panels, debris floating in zero gravity, background showing Earth through a shattered window.

beats.narration: Now zoom out. You see the station as a speck. The nuclear fireball expands. It engulfs the nearby Hubble Space Telescope. The debris cloud spreads. It looks like a golden halo. You watch it choke the sky. The auroras flicker. The satellites burn up. You know what comes next. The Kessler Syndrome. A chain reaction. Every piece of junk becomes a bullet. The orbit is dead. No more launches. No more repairs. No more science. You are stranded. The ground control is silent. The antennas are dead. You check your watch. It says 00:00. It will always say 00:00. The reactor is still hot. It will be hot for a thousand years. The radiation will poison the oceans. The fish will die. The birds will fall. You close your eyes. You imagine the sun. It is still there. You cannot see it. You are in the dark. The dark is forever. You are the last human alive. You are the last thought. You are the last thing. The universe continues. It does not care. You are nothing. You are gone. The space Chernobyl is complete. The lesson is clear. Do not put nuclear reactors in space. Ever. Again.
beats.visual: Wide shot of Earth from deep space, showing a expanding golden debris ring around the planet, auroras flickering irregularly, satellites burning up in the atmosphere, darkening skies, a single red dot representing the dead station.
